head: adfefc0cd53e9e49c0056afe0c0208dc4992dd63
conclusion: No confirmed new bug found in the three-file lifecycle fence and exact-turn status projection patch.
reviewed: Entire production diff and surrounding UnifiedHistory read/publish/error paths, Activity retention/eviction, service lifecycle notifications, metadata observation, accepted start/workflow responses, failure and cleanup branches.

Exact live turn identity projects status without adding absent turns/items or replacing pagination. Unknown state blocks live projection and is never cleared. Stable cold interrupted rows with no live/terminal evidence remain unchanged.
Terminal cache is per Activity and exact turn ID, bounded to one terminal per retained thread. It is cleared for revert/delete/unsubscribe/closed paths and disappears with Activity/runtime lifetime.

Lifecycle revision advances for start/completed notifications, metadata establishing a different active ID, and accepted turn/start or queue/review responses even without notifications. Streaming items and status-only idle updates do not force repeated stale reads.

Traversal binds Activity identity, lifecycle revision, and unknown flag. Changes before publish or between pages reject and delete the old traversal; a fresh no-cursor read can proceed. Initial metadata can establish the first active identity before turn/timeline pages.
Existing channel disconnect, superseding traversal, history invalidation, cursor-loop, item/byte/page limits and incomplete-context barriers remain in place.
Previously reviewed web retry and turn/completed refresh paths remain compatible; no web change is required by this patch.
limitations: No code edits, tests, remote probes, or paid calls performed in this review.
This is a targeted independent diff review, not a new complete repository audit.
Runtime agent owns the deterministic service regression tests; this report does not claim their results.
The original hosted CI failure cause still requires the parent evidence chain; source reasoning and controlled snapshot probes alone do not prove that exact historical execution.

The cache does not synthesize history contents or claim durable item freshness beyond the existing native history contract. Status-only activity without a known turn ID does not revive arbitrary historical turns.
